q.s: A newborn has a vertebral anomaly, an imperforate anus, a ventricular septal defect, a tracheoesophageal fistula, a missing kidney and an absent radius.
cl: a vertebral anomaly, an imperforate anus
a ventricular septal defect, a tracheoesophageal fistula
a missing kidney and an absent radius
q.ch: Vertebral + anal + cardiac + TE fistula + renal + limb defects → VACTERL → mesodermal defect.
q.tr: The notochord's only adult derivative is the nucleus pulposus.
q.q2: Which germ layer is primarily affected?

q.s: A 30-week ultrasound shows excess amniotic fluid and a fetal stomach and duodenum that look like two bubbles. The fetus has features of trisomy 21.
o: The fetus cannot swallow and absorb amniotic fluid past the obstruction
q.ch: Double bubble + polyhydramnios + Down syndrome → duodenal atresia → impaired swallowing and absorption of amniotic fluid.
q.tr: Amniotic fluid comes mainly from fetal urine and is cleared by swallowing.
q.q2: Why is there too much amniotic fluid?

q.s: A newborn has a small, receding jaw, a tongue that falls backward and a U-shaped cleft of the soft palate. He has noisy breathing and trouble feeding. His face is otherwise normal and hearing is normal.
o: Mandibular hypoplasia causing glossoptosis, which prevents palatal shelf fusion
Neural crest dysfunction affecting the zygomatic bones
Failure of the medial nasal process to fuse with the maxillary process
q.k: First and second pharyngeal arch syndromes
cl: U-shaped cleft of the soft palate
q.ch: Micrognathia → glossoptosis → cleft palate and airway obstruction → Pierre Robin sequence.
q.tr: A sequence is a cascade from one primary event.
q.q2: What is the primary event in this condition?

q.s: A 17-year-old girl has never had a menstrual period. Her findings are shown.
cl: has never had a menstrual period
46,XX, normal breasts and ovaries, absent uterus, renal agenesis.
q.ch: 46,XX + normal breasts and ovaries + absent uterus + short vagina + renal agenesis → Müllerian agenesis.
q.tr: Androgen insensitivity looks similar but is 46,XY with scant hair.
q.q2: Which structures failed to develop?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has had three second-trimester miscarriages. A hysterosalpingogram shows a heart-shaped uterine cavity, and MRI shows a deep notch in the outer fundal contour dividing the uterus into two horns.
o: Incomplete resorption of the septum with a normal outer contour
Incomplete fusion of the Müllerian ducts
Failure of the Müllerian ducts to form
cl: deep notch in the outer fundal contour
q.ch: Heart-shaped cavity + indented outer contour → incomplete Müllerian fusion → bicornuate uterus.
q.tr: A septate uterus has a normal outer contour and is treated with septoplasty.
q.q2: What is the embryologic basis?

q.s: A newborn boy has a urethral opening on the underside of the penile shaft, a downward curve of the penis and an undescended left testis.
o: Faulty positioning of the genital tubercle
Failure of the labioscrotal swellings to fuse
Failure of the urethral folds to fuse
cl: on the underside of the penile shaft
a downward curve of the penis
q.ch: Ventral urethral opening + chordee + cryptorchidism → hypospadias → unfused urethral folds.
q.tr: Epispadias is dorsal and associated with bladder exstrophy.
q.q2: What caused the urethral defect?

q.s: During a laparoscopic oophorectomy, the surgeon clamps and divides the ligament containing the ovarian vessels. Two days later the patient has flank pain and fever, and CT shows a dilated ureter on that side.
e: Correct. Suspensory ligament of the ovary.
q.ch: Oophorectomy → ligation of infundibulopelvic ligament (ovarian vessels) near ureter → ureteral injury.
q.tr: Hysterectomy risks ureteral injury at the cardinal ligament (uterine artery).
q.q2: Which ligament was divided?

q.s: A 28-year-old man thrown from a motorcycle has a pelvic fracture. He has blood at the tip of his penis, cannot urinate and his prostate feels high-riding on rectal exam.
e: Wrong. Not the next step for this injury.
cl: blood at the tip of his penis
q.ch: Pelvic fracture + blood at meatus + high-riding prostate → posterior urethral injury → retrograde urethrogram before catheter.
q.tr: Straddle injuries damage the bulbar (anterior) urethra.
q.q2: What is the next step before placing a urinary catheter?

q.s: A 58-year-old man with diabetes has trouble maintaining erections. Nighttime erections are absent. He starts sildenafil, which helps.
o: Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4); NO and cGMP
q.k: Autonomic innervation of male sexual response
q.ch: Erection = parasympathetic (S2–S4) → NO → ↑ cGMP → smooth muscle relaxation; sildenafil blocks cGMP breakdown.
q.tr: "Point (parasympathetic), squeeze (sympathetic), shoot (pudendal)."
q.q2: Which nerves and second messenger mediate erection?

q.s: A 32-year-old tall man comes for infertility after 3 years of trying to conceive. He has small, firm testes, breast enlargement and sparse body hair. His results are shown.
q.ch: Infertility + small firm testes + gynecomastia + high FSH/LH + low testosterone + Barr body → Klinefelter (47,XXY).
q.tr: Increased risk of breast cancer.
q.q2: What is his karyotype?

q.s: A 16-year-old girl is short, has not started breast development and has a heart murmur. Her blood pressure is higher in her arms than her legs. She has a broad chest with widely spaced nipples and a low posterior hairline.
cl: higher in her arms than her legs
q.ch: Short stature + no puberty + coarctation + shield chest → Turner syndrome (45,X) → bicuspid aortic valve.
q.tr: Most common cause of primary amenorrhea.
q.q2: Which cardiac lesion is most associated with her condition?

q.s: A newborn with ambiguous genitalia has a 46,XX karyotype and a normal uterus and ovaries on ultrasound. On day 10 she vomits and has a sodium of 124 mEq/L and potassium of 6.8 mEq/L.
cl: sodium of 124 mEq/L and potassium of 6.8 mEq/L
q.ch: 46,XX virilization + salt wasting → 21-hydroxylase deficiency (most common cause of 46,XX DSD).
q.tr: 17-hydroxyprogesterone is elevated.
q.q2: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
q.fc: Family pedigree. I-1 developed tremor and ataxia at 65; III-1 has intellectual disability. The proband (II-1, arrow) is marked with a dot.

q.s: A 34-year-old woman has not had a period for 10 months and has hot flashes. FSH is 68 mIU/mL and estradiol is low. Her family history is shown.
e: Correct. Fragile X premutation causes primary ovarian insufficiency.
cl: has not had a period for 10 months and has hot flashes
FSH is 68 mIU/mL and estradiol is low
q.ch: Ovarian failure before 40 + father with late tremor/ataxia + son with intellectual disability → fragile X premutation → FMR1 testing.
q.tr: Karyotype screening for Turner mosaicism is also recommended.
q.q2: Which genetic test is most appropriate?
q.fc: Serum hCG and TSH during normal pregnancy

q.s: A 26-year-old woman at 9 weeks has severe vomiting, weight loss and palpitations. Free T4 is mildly elevated and TSH is low. Ultrasound shows a twin pregnancy. Hormone trends in normal pregnancy are shown.
o: High hCG stimulates the TSH receptor, raising T4 and suppressing TSH
q.ch: hCG shares α-subunit and has TSH-like activity → peaks 8–10 weeks (higher with twins) → transient hyperthyroxinemia, low TSH, hyperemesis.
q.tr: Molar pregnancy causes even higher hCG.
q.q2: Why is her TSH low?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman at 32 weeks feels short of breath. Her hemoglobin has fallen from 13 to 10.8 g/dL, her creatinine is 0.5 mg/dL and her ABG shows a mild respiratory alkalosis. Her total thyroxine is high but free T4 is normal.
cl: hemoglobin has fallen from 13 to 10.8 g/dL
total thyroxine is high but free T4 is normal
q.ch: Plasma volume > RBC mass, ↑ GFR, progesterone hyperventilation, ↑ TBG → normal pregnancy.
q.tr: Pregnancy is also a hypercoagulable state.
q.q2: Which explanation fits all these findings?

head: Sign at 5 minutes
Finding
rows: Body pink, hands and feet blue
Some flexion of arms and legs

q.s: A baby is born after a long labor. His findings at 5 minutes are shown.
e: Correct. Appearance 1, Pulse 2, Grimace 2, Activity 1, Respiration 1.
cl: His findings at 5 minutes are shown
q.ch: Appearance (acrocyanosis) 1 + pulse ≥100 2 + grimace (cries, pulls away) 2 + activity (some flexion) 1 + respiration (slow, irregular) 1 = 7.
q.tr: Scores <7 may need further evaluation.
q.q2: What is his Apgar score?

q.s: Two weeks after delivery, a breastfeeding mother asks why her milk flow increases when she hears her baby cry and why she feels cramping when the baby suckles.
e: Wrong. Milk production, not letdown or cramps.
Correct. Milk letdown and uterine contraction.
cl: milk flow increases when she hears her baby cry
feels cramping when the baby suckles
q.ch: Suckling and infant cues → posterior pituitary oxytocin → myoepithelial contraction (letdown) and uterine contraction.
q.tr: Prolactin maintains milk production and suppresses reproductive function.
q.q2: Which hormone explains both effects?
q.fc: Serum FSH and estradiol in one woman followed over 20 years

q.s: A 52-year-old woman has not had a period for 14 months. She has hot flashes, night sweats and vaginal dryness. Her hormone levels over time are shown.
o: Loss of estrogen and inhibin negative feedback as ovarian follicles are depleted
Increased GnRH pulse frequency from PCOS
cl: has not had a period for 14 months
hot flashes, night sweats and vaginal dryness
q.ch: Follicle depletion → ↓ estrogen and inhibin → loss of negative feedback → ↑↑ FSH (specific for menopause).
q.tr: Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency.
q.q2: Why does FSH rise so markedly?

q.s: A 6-year-old girl has breast development, irregular brown skin patches with jagged borders on her back, and a bone lesion in her femur. LH and FSH are suppressed.
e: Wrong. LH and FSH would be high.
q.ch: Precocious puberty + jagged café-au-lait spots + fibrous dysplasia + suppressed gonadotropins → McCune-Albright → peripheral.
q.tr: Caused by a somatic activating GNAS mutation.
q.q2: Which type of precocious puberty is this?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman at 33 weeks has sudden painless bright red vaginal bleeding after intercourse. She had two prior cesarean deliveries. Her uterus is soft and nontender, and the fetal heart rate is normal.
o: Transabdominal ultrasound before any digital cervical exam
Digital cervical exam to check dilation
cl: sudden painless bright red vaginal bleeding
Her uterus is soft and nontender
q.ch: Painless third-trimester bleeding + prior cesareans + soft uterus → placenta previa → ultrasound, avoid digital exam.
q.tr: Abruption is painful with a tender uterus.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A woman whose cord was inserted into the membranes is in labor at term. When her membranes rupture, there is a gush of bright red blood, and the fetal heart rate drops to 70/min. The mother's vital signs are normal.
o: The mother's, from the placental bed
The fetus's, from torn unprotected fetal vessels
The mother's, from a cervical laceration
cl: cord was inserted into the membranes
The mother's vital signs are normal
q.ch: Velamentous insertion + bleeding at membrane rupture + fetal bradycardia → vasa previa → fetal hemorrhage.
q.tr: Fetal death can occur quickly.
q.q2: Whose blood is being lost?

q.s: A woman who had a classical cesarean section 18 months ago is in labor. She suddenly has severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding and loss of fetal station. The fetal heart rate drops and fetal parts are easily palpated under the abdominal wall.
q.ch: Prior cesarean + labor + sudden pain + loss of station + palpable fetal parts + fetal distress → uterine rupture.
q.tr: Emergency laparotomy is required.
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?

q.s: A woman at 34 weeks becomes lightheaded and pale when she lies flat on her back for an ultrasound. Her BP drops from 118/72 to 86/50 mm Hg. Rolling onto her left side relieves her symptoms within a minute.
o: Compression of the IVC and aorta by the gravid uterus
cl: when she lies flat on her back
BP drops from 118/72 to 86/50 mm Hg
q.ch: Gravid uterus compresses IVC and aorta when supine → ↓ venous return and placental perfusion → relieved by left lateral position.
q.tr: Seen after 20 weeks.
q.q2: What is the mechanism?

q.s: A 66-year-old woman has severe vulvar itching for years. The vulvar skin is thin and white like porcelain, and the change extends around the anus in a figure-eight pattern.
o: It is benign but slightly increases the risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma
It occurs only in young women
q.ch: Older woman + porcelain-white vulvar plaques + figure-eight → lichen sclerosus → slight SCC risk.
q.tr: Non-HPV vulvar carcinoma usually arises from lichen sclerosus.
q.q2: Which statement about her condition is correct?

q.s: A 2-year-old girl has vaginal bleeding and a clear, grape-like mass protruding from her vagina. Biopsy shows small spindle-shaped tumor cells that stain for desmin.
q.ch: Young girl + grapelike vaginal mass + desmin-positive spindle cells → sarcoma botryoides.
q.tr: DES exposure causes vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma.
q.q2: What is the diagnosis?

q.s: A 17-year-old girl has crampy lower abdominal pain that starts with her period each month and lasts 2 days. Pelvic exam and ultrasound are normal.
cl: starts with her period each month
Pelvic exam and ultrasound are normal
q.ch: Menstrual cramps with normal pelvic findings → primary dysmenorrhea (prostaglandins) → NSAIDs or hormonal contraceptives.
q.tr: Endometriosis causes secondary dysmenorrhea.
q.q2: What is the first-line treatment?

q.s: A 35-year-old woman has palpitations, heat intolerance and weight loss. TSH is suppressed but her thyroid gland is not enlarged and thyroid uptake in the neck is low. A pelvic scan shows a complex ovarian mass that takes up radioactive iodine.
o: Struma ovarii (monodermal teratoma with thyroid tissue)
cl: thyroid uptake in the neck is low
q.ch: Hyperthyroidism with low neck uptake + ovarian mass taking up iodine → struma ovarii.
q.tr: Mature teratomas contain all three germ layers.
q.q2: What is the diagnosis?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman has developed a deep voice, acne, frontal balding and an enlarged clitoris over 6 months. Serum testosterone is very high, and DHEA-S is normal. A solid right ovarian mass is found.
cl: deep voice, acne, frontal balding and an enlarged clitoris
q.ch: Rapid virilization + high testosterone + normal DHEA-S + ovarian mass → Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor.
q.tr: Resembles testicular histology.
q.q2: Which tumor is most likely?

q.s: A 34-year-old woman had a dilation and curettage for a retained placenta 1 year ago. Since then her periods have been very light, and she cannot conceive. Progestin withdrawal produces no bleeding even after estrogen priming.
cl: dilation and curettage for a retained placenta
no bleeding even after estrogen priming
q.ch: Prior D&C + scant menses + infertility + no withdrawal bleed despite estrogen → Asherman syndrome.
q.tr: Progestin challenge bleeding rules out outflow defects.
q.q2: What is the diagnosis?

q.s: A 23-year-old woman has a firm, rubbery, well-defined 2-cm lump in her left breast that moves easily under the skin. It becomes more tender before her period.
q.ch: Young woman + small mobile well-defined lump + cyclic tenderness → fibroadenoma.
q.tr: Cancer risk is usually not increased.
q.q2: What is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 46-year-old woman has bloody discharge from one nipple. There is no mass. Ultrasound shows a small lesion within a duct just beneath the areola.
cl: within a duct just beneath the areola
q.ch: Unilateral bloody nipple discharge + small subareolar intraductal lesion → intraductal papilloma.
q.tr: Most common cause of nipple discharge.
q.q2: What is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 50-year-old woman's breast became red, warm and swollen over 3 weeks. The skin has a dimpled orange-peel texture. She has no fever, and antibiotics did not help. No discrete mass is felt.
o: Extension of DCIS onto the nipple
cl: red, warm and swollen over 3 weeks
q.ch: Erythematous swollen breast + peau d'orange + no response to antibiotics → inflammatory carcinoma → dermal lymphatic invasion.
q.tr: Poor prognosis (about 50% 5-year survival).
q.q2: What is the mechanism of the skin change?

q.s: A 16-year-old boy with sickle cell disease has had a painful erection for 5 hours. The shaft is rigid but the glans is soft.
o: Sickled red cells obstruct venous drainage of the corpora cavernosa
Fibrous plaque in the tunica albuginea
q.ch: Sickle cell disease → sickled RBCs block cavernosal venous outflow → painful ischemic priapism → aspiration, phenylephrine.
q.tr: Trazodone and sildenafil can also cause priapism.
q.q2: What is the mechanism?

q.s: A 24-year-old man has a small testicular mass, enlarged tender breasts, palpitations and coughing up blood. His results are shown.
q.ch: Testicular mass + very high hCG + gynecomastia + hyperthyroid features + early lung metastases → choriocarcinoma.
q.tr: Hematogenous spread to lungs and brain.
q.q2: What is the most likely tumor?

q.s: A 67-year-old man has painless swelling of both testes. Biopsy shows sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells.
q.ch: Older man + bilateral testicular masses + lymphoid cells → primary testicular lymphoma (most common testicular cancer >60).
q.tr: Seminoma is the most common in young men.
q.q2: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 25-year-old competitive bodybuilder and his wife have been unable to conceive. He has acne, breast enlargement and small testes, and his wife says he has become irritable and aggressive. His results are shown.
o: Exogenous androgens suppressing GnRH, LH and FSH
Primary testicular failure from Klinefelter syndrome
Congenital absence of the vas deferens
e: Wrong. LH and FSH would be high.
cl: acne, breast enlargement and small testes
q.ch: High hematocrit + bad lipids + suppressed LH/FSH + azoospermia + small testes + gynecomastia → exogenous androgens → ↓ intratesticular testosterone.
q.tr: Recovery after stopping is slow.
q.q2: What is the cause of his infertility?

q.s: A 70-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer has disease progression despite castration-level testosterone. He starts a drug that inhibits CYP17. Two months later he has hypertension, edema and a potassium of 2.9 mEq/L.
q.ch: CYP17 inhibition blocks androgen and cortisol synthesis → ACTH rises → mineralocorticoid excess → hypertension, hypokalemia (given with prednisone).
q.tr: Ketoconazole also inhibits 17α-hydroxylase.
q.q2: Which drug was started?

q.s: A 58-year-old woman with osteoporosis and a strong family history of breast cancer wants a drug that will protect her bones and lower her breast cancer risk without increasing her risk of endometrial cancer. She does not smoke and has no history of blood clots.
cl: without increasing her risk of endometrial cancer
q.ch: Bone agonist + breast and uterine antagonist → raloxifene ("relax").
q.tr: All SERMs raise thromboembolic risk.
q.q2: Which drug is best?

q.s: A 36-year-old woman who smokes 15 cigarettes a day and has migraines with visual aura wants reliable, reversible contraception. She does not want hormones in her body if possible.
q.ch: Smoker >35 + migraine with aura → avoid estrogen → copper IUD (hormone-free, local inflammation toxic to sperm and ova).
q.tr: Copper IUD can increase menstrual bleeding.
q.q2: Which method is most appropriate?

q.s: A 62-year-old man has urinary hesitancy and a weak stream from BPH. He takes medicines for hypertension and had dizziness on terazosin. He wants rapid symptom relief.
o: Tamsulosin; it selectively blocks α1A/D receptors in the prostate, causing less hypotension
Oxybutynin; it relaxes the bladder neck
cl: urinary hesitancy and a weak stream from BPH
Orthostatic hypotension from nonselective α1 blockade.
q.ch: BPH needing quick relief + intolerance of nonselective α1-blocker → tamsulosin (α1A/D-selective).
q.tr: Finasteride shrinks the gland over months.
q.q2: Which drug is best, and why?
